title: Joint attention is either following someone's focus or starting it
summary: Mundy and Newell describe two infant joint-attention acts: following another person's gaze or gesture, and using one's own gesture or look to direct them.
body: Peter Mundy and Lisa Newell say joint attention is coordinating attention with a partner. They split infant behavior into responding and initiating. Responding means following the direction of someone else's gaze and gestures to share a reference point. Initiating means using gestures and eye contact to direct the other person toward an object, an event, or oneself, in order to show or share interest. They also say infants follow other people's gaze in the first year, and that sharing a reference point comes before language. This is their review's definition, not a screening score and not a claim that the two acts always rise together.

sources.title: Attention, joint attention, and social cognition
sources.author: Peter Mundy and Lisa Newell
sources.note: Supports the definitions of responding to joint attention and initiating joint attention, including the sharing function of initiating. Peer-reviewed open copy.
